name: IN-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+16 partisan lean in a northeast Indiana seat
Incumbent Stutzman renominated with a large fundraising edge
No public polling and no expert ratings to shift the picture
model.rationale: The district's R+16 lean, Stutzman's incumbency and roughly six-to-one fundraising advantage, and Polymarket pricing the Democrat at about 6% all point the same direction, with no polls or headlines suggesting an upset. The forecast stays near the fundamentals-based estimate, slightly beyond the raw lean to reflect the incumbent's position.
model.watch: Any late independent polling or unexpected outside spending against Stutzman would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northeast Indiana's third district is a strongly Republican seat, with a partisan lean of about sixteen points toward the GOP. Marlin Stutzman returns as the incumbent after winning renomination, giving Republicans both the structural and experience advantages. Kelly Thompson, the Democratic nominee, is a first-time challenger with modest resources.

The money gap is stark: Stutzman has raised roughly $840,000 to Thompson's $136,000, and he holds most of the cash on hand, with a small amount of outside support on his side and none opposing him. No public general-election polls exist for the race, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive. Prediction markets give the Democrat only about a six percent chance. All available evidence points to a comfortable Republican hold.
